interpretation: The critical default control flow is now executable, not only statically inferred. The exact top-level source reloads the exact base source per operation; the exact base source reloads the exact attempt module per operation; the exact attempt module generates _BOOT_SECRET at import. Therefore a permit produced on RESERVE is rejected before scorer execution when SCORE uses a fresh attempt-module instance. Reusing one exact attempt-module instance across RESERVE and SCORE removes the liveness defect, while a fresh epoch rejects the old permit and the durable reservation remains fail-closed/no-relaunch.
scope_limitations: This A/B executed the exact bytes of the three modules that create the reload/HMAC defect, but replaced noncritical sibling semantics with deterministic stubs. It is stronger than static source reasoning but is not a complete exact-sibling lifecycle execution.
The process-stable arm is an injection-equivalent of ProcessStableRuntimeContext's core repair, not a byte-execution of the full context load() over all manifest siblings.
No deployment or distributed-fencing claim is made.
measurement_validity_rules: Treat import-time secret/state identity as part of the runtime contract whenever permits or evidence bindings depend on process-local state.
A default-path test must count scorer invocations; fail-closed permit rejection with scorer_calls=0 is a liveness failure, not a false-evidence event.
A repair must preserve the cross-epoch rejection property. Within-epoch continuity and cross-epoch invalidation are both required.
